'''Yuga Shrine''' (瑜伽神社) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en|Shinto shrine|qid=Q845945|lt=Shinto shrine}} located in {{ill|Takabatakechō|ja|高畑町|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Takabatake Town|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q24899934}}, {{ill|Nara (city)|en|Nara (city)|qid=Q169134|lt=Nara}}, {{ill|Nara Prefecture|en|Nara Prefecture|qid=Q131287|lt=Nara Prefecture}}, on Yuga Mountain.

== History ==
According to shrine tradition, the sacred mountain {{ill|Asuka Kannabi|ja|飛鳥神奈備|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Asuka Kannabi|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} was relocated to this site with the establishment of {{ill|Heijō-kyō|en|Heijō-kyō|qid=Q862509|lt=Heijō-kyō}}, and the mountain was subsequently called the Asuka Mountain of Heijō{{sfn|Nara City History: Shrines and Temples|p=81}}. Initially, the shrine served as the guardian of {{ill|Gangō-ji|en|Gangō-ji|qid=Q1203099|lt=Gango-ji}} {{ill|Q104539457|ja|禅定院|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Zenjō-in|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q104539457}}, protecting against misfortune from the {{ill|Kimon|ja|鬼門|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kimon|qq=}} direction. Later, when {{ill|Daijō-in|ja|大乗院|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Daijō-in|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q16766994}} of {{ill|Kōfuku-ji|en|Kōfuku-ji|qid=Q1070863|lt=Kōfuku-ji}} was built at the foot of the mountain, the shrine was venerated by the {{ill|Fujiwara clan|en|Fujiwara clan|qid=Q641628|lt=Fujiwara clan}} and others{{sfn|Nara City History: Shrines and Temples|p=81}}.

The ''{{ill|Daijōin Jisha Zōjiki|ja|大乗院寺社雑事記|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Daijō-in Jisha Zasshiki|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11432101}}'' records an entry from December 30, 1494, stating "Ichigo Chieko-in-den Go-kenchiku no Bun ... Imamiyaden Goten Dō Haiden Kari-fuki ya," identifying "Imamiya" as referring to this shrine. It is said that "Imamiya" was used in contrast to the original shrine in Asuka{{sfn|Nara City History: Shrines and Temples|p=81}}. The current name, Yuga Shrine, has been in use only relatively recently{{sfn|Nara City History: Shrines and Temples|p=81}}.

== Cultural Properties ==
=== Yuga Mountain Cherry and Maple Monument ===
<blockquote>
In spring, the flowers bloom again upon Yuga Mountain.
Today’s autumn leaves, one hesitates to part from.
</blockquote>
The poem was composed by {{ill|Yoshiki Kajino|ja|梶野良材|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kajino Yoshitaka|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11538933}}, also known as Kajino Tosa-no-kami Fujiwara no Yoshitaka. He served as the {{ill|Ongoku-bugyō|ja|奈良奉行|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nara Magistrate|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 遠国奉行|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q17171698}} from April 8, 1831, until his transfer as the Kyoto West Magistrate on December 8, 1837. He also authored ''{{ill|Yamashiro Yamato Kenbun Zuihitsu|ja|山城大和見聞随筆|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yamashiro Yamato Kenbun Zuihitsu|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}'' ("An Essay on Observations in Yamashiro and Yamato").

Yuga Mountain has been famous for its cherry blossoms and autumn foliage since ancient times and is included among the {{ill|Sixteen Views of Nara|ja|奈良十六景|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sixteen Views of Nara|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, featuring "Yuga Mountain Cherry Blossoms" and "Yuga Mountain Autumn Leaves"{{sfn|Nara City History: Shrines and Temples|p=80}}.

=== "Asuka of Heijō" Manyō Poem Monument ===
<blockquote>
The Asuka of my old home is now in ruin,
Yet fair is Asuka of Nara,
How beautiful it remains.
</blockquote>
This poem was composed by {{ill|Ōtomo no Sakanoue no Iratsume|en|Ōtomo no Sakanoue no Iratsume|qid=Q839976|lt=Ōtomo no Sakanoue no Iratsume}} in the fifth year of {{ill|Tenpyō|en|Tenpyō|qid=Q1199879|lt=Tenpyō}}, corresponding to 733 CE.

== Access ==
* By train: The shrine is accessible from {{ill|Kintetsu Nara Station|en|Kintetsu Nara Station|qid=Q6414371|lt=Kintetsu Nara Station}}, followed by a short walk.
* By car: Parking is available near the shrine grounds.
